title: Many copies, how many sources?
hook: Compare two message trees whose endorsements all originate from one source.

knows: basic arithmetic and how to compare two stated rules
doesNotKnow: how to distinguish message reach from the number of independent information origins

misconception: A dozen repeated endorsements necessarily represent a dozen independent observations.
objective: Distinguish message reach from the number of independent information origins.

claims.text: Original stipulated tree model: Source at round 0. In each following round, each newly reached node sends to two previously unused nodes. The first case uses one recipient instead. Count the source and all descendants once; cap total at twelve. No overlaps, credibility, persuasion or behavior model. Scenario A (one recipient) reaches 1+1+1+1=4 nodes; scenario B (two recipients) reaches min(12,1+2+4+8)=12 nodes. Prediction premise: Starting with one source at round 0, each newly reached node sends to two unused nodes next round. After three rounds, including the source and capped at 12, how many nodes? One-recipient forwarding reaches {A}; two-recipient forwarding {B}. Extra branches multiply copies, while the original source remains one.
